description: Four low-frequency oscillators sharing one phase and spread around the cycle, with a shape control morphing through sine, triangle, sawtooth, square and a random walk

params.text: Morphs the wave through sine, triangle, sawtooth, square and a random walk, blending between neighbours all the way
Sets how far a Lorenz attractor pulls each output's phase, level and rate about; fully clockwise leaves the waves clean and turning it down lets them wander, each output on its own attractor
Sets the rate, about 0.03Hz at one end of the travel to about 10Hz at the other, shown in hertz on the tooltip
Spreads the four outputs around the cycle: fully anticlockwise puts all four in phase and fully clockwise puts them a quarter cycle apart
Sets how far every output swings either side of the centre, 0 to 5V

inputs.text: Changes the shape, scaled by a tenth and added to the shape knob, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the stability, scaled by a tenth and added to the stability knob, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Sets the rate from the time between two rises, in place of the frequency knob, and snaps output A's phase back to the start on each rise; the panel prints FREQ but the maker's port name is Clock
Changes the phase spread, scaled by a tenth and added to the spread knob, the total clamped to the knob's travel
Shifts every output, added to the centre knob and clamped to -5 to 5V
Changes how far every output swings, added to the swing knob and clamped to 0 to 5V

outputs.text: The lowest of the four outputs at each moment
The highest of the four outputs at each moment
One of the four waves, centred and scaled by the two spread controls

notes: patching the clock jack takes the rate away from the frequency knob and measures it from the cable instead, holding it between 0.1Hz and 100Hz
